pieces.t: The New Hampshire Journeyman Electrician examination is part of the state electrical licensing process. Candidates preparing for this exam should follow the current application and testing instructions connected to New Hampshire electrical licensing before scheduling. pieces.h: Exam Details
pieces.t: New Hampshire journeyman electrician preparation should include the National Electrical Code, electrical theory, practical installation knowledge, conductor sizing, grounding and bonding, services, feeders, branch circuits, motors, transformers, wiring methods, raceways, boxes, overcurrent protection, special occupancies, special equipment, safety, and calculations. Candidates should also be prepared to review New Hampshire-specific electrical rules and licensing responsibilities when those topics are included in the exam materials or application instructions. Electrical calculations are an important part of journeyman-level preparation. Candidates should practice service load calculations, feeder calculations, branch-circuit calculations, conductor ampacity, conductor adjustment and correction, voltage drop, box fill, raceway fill, motor calculations, transformer calculations, demand factors, neutral loads, continuous loads, and overcurrent protection sizing. Calculation questions can be challenging under time pressure, so repeated practice is a key part of preparation.

pieces.h: Licensing Steps
pieces.t: The New Hampshire master electrician licensing process begins with confirming the correct license classification. Candidates pursuing the Master Electrician license should review the Electricians’ Board requirements for experience, application eligibility, examination approval, and license issuance before applying. Before applying for the master examination, candidates must meet the journeyman-to-master qualification path. New Hampshire requires master electrician applicants to have passed the journeyman examination and obtained 2,000 hours of field experience as a journeyman in electrical installations before taking the master examination. Candidates should organize documentation showing their license history and qualifying field experience. Once the candidate is ready to apply, the appropriate application is submitted through the New Hampshire Office of Professional Licensure and Certification process. The Electricians’ Board reviews the application and determines whether the candidate is eligible to test.

The Electricians’ Board within the New Hampshire Office of Professional Licensure and Certification develops and maintains professional standards for electrician licensure. Candidates pursuing a New Hampshire Master Electrician license should follow the state licensing process rather than a local-only license path.
